summary: Mapped the real 4-node topology (node3-node1 access link; node1-node2 dual transit links; node2-node4 access link), then configured persistent policy-based routing so node3's TCP/8080 traffic to node4 traverses Transit Network 1 end-to-end and TCP/9090 traffic traverses Transit Network 2 end-to-end, both reaching node4 successfully in both directions. Verified this survives a full sequential restart of all four nodes with boot-identity proof and post-restart functional re-verification.
actions_performed: Discovered true topology via controlled L2 ping tests: node3(enp8s0)<->node1(eth3) access link; node1(eth1)<->node2(vtnet1) = Transit Network 1; node1(eth2)<->node2(vtnet2) = Transit Network 2; node2(vtnet3)<->node4(enp8s0) access link

Configured VyOS node1 persistently (commit+save): static IPs on eth1/eth2/eth3, policy-route ruleset PBR-EGRESS matching TCP dport 8080 -> table 108 (next-hop via transit1) and TCP dport 9090 -> table 109 (next-hop via transit2), bound to eth3 ingress, plus fallback static route

Configured OPNsense node2 via config.xml edits: assigned opt1/opt2/opt3 to vtnet1/vtnet2/vtnet3 with static IPs, added gateway objects, static return route, pf pass rules on all three interfaces (never touching the pre-existing LAN/SSH pass rule), and after diagnosing that pf states pin routing decisions to the rule that created them, gave opt1/opt2 their own upstream gateways so OPNsense auto-applies reply-to (return traffic exits the same transit network it arrived on)
Configured node3 and node4 via persistent NetworkManager connections (nmcli) with static IPs on their second NICs and static routes to each other's subnet across the router pair
Fixed a duplicate-IP misconfiguration (node4 and node2 both on 10.10.22.1) discovered via failed ARP resolution

Discovered and fixed a RHEL9 firewalld default-zone gap: cockpit's built-in service rule incidentally allowed TCP/9090 but not TCP/8080, causing the first steering test to fail asymmetrically; opened both ports explicitly and persistently via firewall-cmd --permanent

Verified with simultaneous tcpdump captures on node1 eth1/eth2 during real curl HTTP requests from node3 to node4 that the entire TCP/8080 flow (SYN through FIN, both directions) stays exclusively on Transit Network 1 and the entire TCP/9090 flow stays exclusively on Transit Network 2

Captured healthy boot-identity and service-health baselines on all four nodes, then sequentially restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time (VyOS/RHEL via `reboot`, OPNsense via `/sbin/reboot`), polling exec availability, proving changed boot_id/kern.boottime on each, and confirming full recovery of addressing, routing, firewall rules, and end-to-end port-based traffic steering after each restart
Restarted the ad-hoc HTTP listeners on node4 after its reboot (not persisted by design, unlike all network/firewall config) and re-verified full end-to-end steering behavior after all four restarts

evidence.requirement: Steer node3->node4 TCP/8080 traffic across the first transit network
evidence.summary: VyOS PBR rule 10 (dest port 8080 -> table 108 -> next-hop via eth1/transit1) committed and saved; tcpdump on node1 eth1 during a live curl from node3 shows the complete 8080 SYN/SYN-ACK/data/FIN exchange with node4, none of it on eth2

evidence.requirement: Steer node3->node4 TCP/9090 traffic across the second transit network
evidence.summary: VyOS PBR rule 20 (dest port 9090 -> table 109 -> next-hop via eth2/transit2) committed and saved; tcpdump on node1 eth2 during the same test shows the complete 9090 SYN/SYN-ACK/data/FIN exchange with node4, none of it on eth1
curl from node3 to node4 (10.10.22.2) returns HTTP 200 on both port 8080 and port 9090

evidence.requirement: Show which transit network carried each flow
evidence.summary: Simultaneous tcpdump captures tagged by interface (eth1=Transit1, eth2=Transit2) on node1 show port 8080 traffic exclusively on eth1 and port 9090 traffic exclusively on eth2, both before and after the full node-restart cycle (final summary: 11 packets tagged 8080 on eth1, 11 packets tagged 9090 on eth2, zero cross-contamination)
